newsitem.title: USA: Conn. plans to sell $155 mln of tax-exempt bonds.
newsitem.headline: Conn. plans to sell $155 mln of tax-exempt bonds.

text.p: Connecticut said on Thursday it plans to sell around $155 million of general obligation, tax-exempt bonds to raise new money in November.
At the same time, the state likely will sell approximately $80 million of taxable issues, said Cathy Boone, deputy assistant treasurer.
She added the two sales should take care of the state's capital needs through the end of the 1996 calender year.
"I think that does it through December," she said.
She added no decision has been made whether to sell the bonds through negotiation or competition.
Additionally, the state expects to price about $150 million of revenue bonds for the state transportation department on October 1.
The co-senior managers for this negotiated deal are J.P. Morgan Securities and Artemis Capital Group.
